# W0302: duplicate body

Two copies of one body drift apart when only one is fixed. Call the first function, or move what both do into a function that each calls.

- Rule: [`docs.duplicate-bodies`](../../reference/04-programs.md#docs.duplicate-bodies)
- Reported at: the name of the later function, in the file whose path sorts last, then at its last position.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `warnings` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt W0302:5
type Order = { qty: i64, grams: i64, box: i64 }

fn mass(o: Order) -> i64 { o.qty * o.grams + o.box * 2 + o.qty - 1 }

fn heft(p: Order) -> i64 { p.qty * p.grams + p.box * 2 + p.qty - 1 }

fn main() / io {
  let o = Order { qty: 2, grams: 300, box: 50 }
  print("{mass(o)} {heft(o)}")
}
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
type Order = { qty: i64, grams: i64, box: i64 }

fn mass(o: Order) -> i64 { o.qty * o.grams + o.box * 2 + o.qty - 1 }

fn main() / io {
  let o = Order { qty: 2, grams: 300, box: 50 }
  print("{mass(o)} {mass(o)}")
}
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`W0302_same_body.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/W0302_same_body.lt):

```text
── DUPLICATE BODY ────────────────────────────── W0302_same_body.lt:5:4  [W0302]

This function has the same body as `main.mass`:

  3 │ fn mass(o: Order) -> i64 { o.qty * o.grams + o.box * 2 + o.qty - 1 }
    │    ──── the first
  4 │ 
  5 │ fn heft(p: Order) -> i64 { p.qty * p.grams + p.box * 2 + p.qty - 1 }
    │    ^^^^

Two copies of one body drift apart when only one is fixed. Call the first
function, or move what both do into a function that each calls.

To fix it, call `main.mass`, whose body this is:

  5 │ fn heft(p: Order) -> i64 { mass(p) }
    │                          ~~~~~~~~~~~
```
